name: JavaScript

levelNotes.5: Good depth topics: closures and scope, prototype chain, iterators/generators, Promise ordering (microtasks vs macrotasks), WeakMap.
levelNotes.7: Good depth topics: async concurrency limits, cancellation with AbortSignal, Proxy/Reflect, event-loop ordering puzzles.
levelNotes.8: Good depth topics: tiny interpreters, reactive signals, virtual-DOM diff, scheduler with priorities.

image.dockerfile:
FROM node:24-slim
WORKDIR /opt/eco
RUN npm init -y >/dev/null && npm install --no-audit --no-fund typescript@5.8.3 vitest@2.1.9 fastify@5.2.1 zod@3.23.8 && npm cache clean --force && ln -s /opt/eco/node_modules/.bin/tsc /usr/local/bin/tsc

ecosystem.conventions: Tests use vitest 2.1 (describe/it/expect, it.each, vi.fn, vi.spyOn, vi.useFakeTimers) in tests/*.test.{mjs,ts}; they load the code under test from ../$TARGET/ with a dynamic import, written EXACTLY like this because Vite only resolves template-string imports one level deep (bugs/<name>/ is two): `const target = new URL(`../${process.env.TARGET ?? "starter"}/solution.mjs`, import.meta.url).href; const { fn } = await import(/* @vite-ignore */ target);` (use solution.ts for TypeScript). Libraries resolve from the test run's node_modules (already set up by the test command): import them normally. zod 3.23 is available for validation; use it where a professional would validate untrusted input. A plausible 'alternative' bug is often a hand-rolled check with different semantics than the schema, or a mock that hides a real bug.
